=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:179-214 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `_family_word` loses subcommands when a global option with a separate value precedes them, causing distinct commands such as `gh -R owner/repo api` and `gh -R owner/repo issue view` to share the family word `gh`.
  WHY: Permission-prompt reports for distinct subcommands can be filed as comments on the same unrelated family issue instead of being tracked separately.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:136, 408-413, 520-522 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: An unescaped logged command containing a four-or-more-backtick fence followed by a family marker can prematurely terminate the example-block match, leaving the marker outside the removed example.
  WHY: On a legacy issue without a generated family marker, `index_issues` can trust the forged marker and route later prompts to the wrong issue; reviewers describe practical exploitability as narrow.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:697-727 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Concurrent `file_patterns` invocations can each read an empty family index and create a separate issue for the same family.
  WHY: Issue creation neither reserves the family nor rechecks the index after posting, so concurrent reports can produce duplicate family issues; reviewers note this is a pre-existing race and stage sessions are usually sequential.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:312-322 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_family_core` unconditionally skips a token after processing `timeout` flags, so `timeout -k 5 git fetch` loses `git` from the family core.
  WHY: The attempted command is logged even when malformed `timeout` usage errors, and family classification can consequently route it to the wrong family issue.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  PROBLEM: `_family_word` loses subcommands when a value-taking global option such as `-R owner/repo` precedes them, causing different `gh` operations to receive family word `gh`.

- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: file_patterns at 697-727 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Concurrent `file_patterns` invocations can each observe an empty family index and create an issue for the same family.
  WHY: The family path does not reserve the family or recheck the index after posting; the reviewer notes this is a pre-existing race with low practical likelihood due to serial stage execution.
